title: A signed-direction invariant for triangle tilings, and the exclusion of primes congruent to 3 modulo 4
description: Erdos problem 634 asks for the set of N such that some triangle can be cut into N pairwise congruent triangles. A folklore conjecture holds that no prime N congruent to 3 modulo 4 with N > 3 occurs. This work proves that conjecture. The main paper introduces a translation-invariant signed-direction functional: weighting a directed edge of direction j*(pi/3) + k*alpha by length times (-1)^j makes interior contributions cancel even across non-edge-to-edge incidences, so the sum over tiles equals the same functional on the boundary. On the isosceles 2pi/3 target this excludes every prime tile count, where previously only a finite lower bound was known. A self-contained reduction handles the scalene shapes, and machine-checked propositions replace Beeson's Theorems 18 and 20, whose printed proofs are unsound. The remaining branch, the base-beta family N = 3f^2 - e^2 with gcd(e,f) = 1 and 1 <= e < f (the primes congruent to 11 modulo 12), is excluded by a forcing chain given in a companion note: boundary-walk trichotomy, corner, partner and strip forcing, the surplus lattice, the column-filler recursion with its orientation congruences, the feet budget, and the T_mid and pentagon kills. In particular no triangle can be cut into 19 congruent triangles. The only published exclusion in that branch, Beeson's Theorem 14, rests on a divisibility g | M shown here to be false, refuted by an explicit 99-tiling. On the constructive side the work exhibits and certifies tilings into 28, 44, 77 and 99 congruent triangles, the 44-tiling of the isosceles (16,16,22) by the (2,3,4) tile being the smallest known tiling in an incommensurable branch, and gives an explicit construction of the unit parallelogram for every member of the e = 1 family, verified for f = 2 through 12. Combined with a collar induction this determines a complete instance spectrum for the first time in such a branch: for the tile (2,3,4) on its isosceles target, N = 11m^2 is realizable exactly for m not equal to 1. For e >= 2 the corresponding parallelogram is shown not to exist, so the branch splits. The admissible spectrum of each sporadic 2pi/3 branch is determined, membership in the tile-count set is shown to be decidable, and the contiguous initial segment of the spectrum is settled. Related to the constructions of Zhang, the parallelogram lemma underlying them is shown to be sharp, and his sufficiency conjecture is confirmed by exhaustive search at three instances below the bound of his own method. The arithmetic and combinatorial layer is machine-checked in Lean 4 (38 files, no sorry): the tiling certificates and combinatorial cores are dependency-free kernel computations, the rest is checked against Mathlib v4.30.0. The geometric layer of the forcing chain rests on written proofs, there being no theory of triangle dissections in Mathlib. The work has not been independently refereed and is presented for peer review.
